data.name: Divyanshay
data.long_meaning: Divyanshay is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'divya' meaning divine and 'ansh' meaning auspicious or part. This name symbolizes the divine presence in an individual.

in_sanskrit.name: दिव्यंशय
in_sanskrit.meaning: दिव्य (Divy) - divine, अंश (Ansh) - grace, हय (Hay) - horse
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who has divine grace and the power of a horse.

in_hindi.name: दिव्यंश
in_hindi.meaning: दिव्य (Divy) - दिव्यता (divine), अंश (Ansh) - अनुपमा (grace), ह (H) - हाथ (hand), य (Y) - यहुः (Yahu) - ईश्वर (Ishvar) - God
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one who has the divine grace of God in his hand.

in_tamil.name: திவ்யங்சய

in_tamil.long_meaning: The one who has the divine grace of a horse.

historical_references.reference: Divyanshay was a renowned Rajput king of the Chauhan dynasty who ruled in the 12th century. He is best known for his victory over the Muslim sultan Muhammad of Ghor at the Second Battle of Tarain in 1191, which marked a significant turning point in the history of the Indian subcontinent with the repulsion of the initial Muslim invasion.
